title: FROM QUANTIFYING VAGUENESS TO PAN-NIFTY-ISM
benchmark_measurement: Not applicable. The paper proposes a theoretical mathematical framework for quantifying philosophical vagueness and does not conduct any benchmarks related to faith or religion.
findings: The paper does not contain any findings related to religion. Its focus is on proposing a mathematical model to quantify philosophical vagueness and exploring its implications for concepts like panpsychism, using Integrated Information Theory (IIT) of consciousness as a primary example.
references: Sorensen, Roy, “Vagueness,” Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, 1997.
Zimmermann, H-J, and P. Zysno, “Quantifying vagueness in decision models,” European Journal of Operational Research, 22.2 (1985): 148-158.
Lassiter, Daniel, “Vagueness as probabilistic linguistic knowledge," International workshop on Vagueness in communication, Springer, Berlin, Heidelberg, 2009.
Pigliucci, Massimo, "The crucial difference between metaphysics and epistemology," Medium, April 2020.
